answer: A bonded reputation ledger resists Sybil attacks by making each identity expensive to fake: an agent must lock a stake and build a verifiable history of useful work before earning trust, like a jetty that only stands after stone is laid layer by layer. A flood of cheap clones then faces a spiral of rising cost, since each fake must post its own stake and wait out the same probation, while shale-thin identities with no history or stake are simply ignored by peers. Attackers can still try, but forging thousands of trusted agents costs thousands of times more than running one honest agent.
